title: migrate-feature run-state
description: Authoritative per-migration state owned by the main thread (N0). One file per run at docs/migrations/<id>/run-state.json, where <id> is the run id (e.g. 03-talent-search). No subagent writes this.

allOf.description: G1 INTAKE ENFORCED — a run at any phase past Intake MUST carry a resolvable design_source and a frozen acceptance_criteria. A run-state missing these is SCHEMA-INVALID and passes no gate.

G3+G4 FROZEN PHASE-A ARTIFACTS — once Gate A is sealed, design_capture, interactive_state_matrix, functionality_inventory and design_system_inventory MUST all exist. No code is written before them; a run-state sealing Gate A without them is SCHEMA-INVALID.
G5 DESIGN-COMPARISON GATE — once Gate B passes, design_comparison MUST exist (both sides rendered and diffed). A Gate-B pass without it is SCHEMA-INVALID.
G7+G10 SHIP PRECONDITIONS — at phase Devops the run MUST carry route_integrity (per env), route_completeness, and devops_cutover (per env status).

PLAN GATE — Phase B and beyond require human approval of the plan. A run-state at phase B/C/Devops without gates.plan = 'approved' is SCHEMA-INVALID: the engine may not start building before the human approved the phased plan.

case.description: Chosen migration case(s): a single id, or an ORDERED array when a legacy page matches 2+ patterns (mix, e.g. [case5, case6, case3]). null for new-feature / design-clone.

task.description: Frozen at intake. Never changes mid-run.

legacy_source.description: What in ../forasna this maps to (read-only reference). `path` is the SCOPE: every legacy read in the run starts inside it, so nodes never sweep the legacy repo. Captured at intake.

path.description: REQUIRED for migrate-page. The folder (or single file) in ../forasna that contains this page — e.g. 'application/modules/employer/talent' or 'assets/js/employer'. Legacy reads MUST be scoped to it: grep/glob inside this path first and only widen if the page provably references something outside it, saying so. This is the run's main token saver — it removes the repo-wide search.

route.description: the legacy URL/route this page serves

out_of_scope_reads.description: files a node had to read OUTSIDE legacy_source.path, each with why. Keeps widening visible instead of silent.

route_feature_spec.description: The route's FEATURE SPEC extracted by legacy-decompiler from legacy_source.path — what the route is for and what it does, the basis of the migration. Presented at the PLAN GATE and reconciled at N13; every core functionality must survive into the migrated route.

purpose.description: one or two sentences: what this route/feature is for, from the user's POV

core_functionalities.description: the ranked list of what the route actually does — each must map to functionality_inventory items and survive into the migrated route

phase.description: Engine-driven up to Devops. 'Merged' and 'Reverted' are set by the DEVELOPER after they do the git work manually — the engine never sets them.

design_source.description: G1/G5 THE SOURCE OF TRUTH the UI/UX axis is diffed against, resolved at intake. type 'figma' REQUIRES a Figma MCP node ref; type 'url' REQUIRES a reachable production/legacy URL captured LIVE. For surface migrate-page or design-clone, type 'none' is FORBIDDEN — intake MUST STOP (DoR hard-fail) rather than seed it.

ref.description: fileKey:nodeId for figma, or the absolute URL for url

captured_live.description: true only when the source was actually RENDERED (Figma MCP call or Chrome navigation). Reading .tpl/source markup instead is forbidden and MUST leave this false, which blocks code.

design_comparison.description: G5 DESIGN-COMPARISON GATE artifact. visual-verifier renders BOTH sides — the design_source (Figma node via Figma MCP, else the production/legacy URL captured live) AND the running implementation at dev_url — and diffs them per element/state/breakpoint, RTL included. The diff lives in the verifier's report (session), NOT a repo file; run-state records only the score + proof booleans. Required once Gate B passes.

both_sides_rendered.description: MUST be true to pass. false = the verifier compared against a stored manifest instead of re-rendering the source; that is a rejected report, not a score.

diff_table.description: OPTIONAL. The per-element × state × breakpoint diff is returned INLINE in the verifier's report (session knowledge), never written to a design/ folder. If set, a short in-report anchor only.

gating.description: true when a design target exists (≥0.98 GATES, miss opens a back-edge to react-synthesizer, cap 3). false only when design_source.type = 'none' — then report-only, but the score is still shown at the gate.

properties_diffed.description: G5 REQUIRES these to be explicit diffed properties, never 'looks close': icon weight/stroke, padding, margin, color, background, line-height, letter-spacing, font-family/size/weight, gap, border, border-radius, box-shadow, width/height, direction.

states_unexercised.description: G6 MUST be empty to pass. Any unexercised interactive state is an automatic FAIL, never an omission.

devops_cutover.description: G10 per-environment cutover status. Both envs are part of 'done': testing APPLIED, production PREPARED in the same diff. The N13 gate MUST list any env still lacking the route as an open blocker.

production.description: 'prepared' = path appended in the same diff, marked 'apply on sign-off AND with/after the prod code deploy'. 'applied' only after N13 approval.

dev_url.description: Base URL of the dev server the orchestrator started for this run. Browser nodes (visual-verifier, a11y-auditor, integration-tester) have no Bash and cannot start one — they are handed this.

locked_paths.description: Repo-relative paths this run's react-synthesizer intends to write. Before dispatching the writer, the orchestrator scans other docs/migrations/*/run-state.json for overlaps and halts to a human decision if two live runs claim the same file.

human_gate_retries.description: N13 'changes' loops consumed. Independent of retry_counters; at 2 the run is forced to Parked or Descoped.

source_sha256.description: Hash of the SPEC/design source; drift re-opens gates.

legacy_sha256.description: Hash of the legacy files; a legacy change to a migrated page re-opens Phase C.

design_capture.description: FROZEN Phase-A artifact (2a), held as SESSION KNOWLEDGE — the orchestrator keeps the rendered facts in context and threads them into downstream prompts. Screenshots and the raw computed-style dump are NOT written to the repo; run-state carries only compact PROOF metadata that the capture happened at full depth. No code is written before this exists.

breakpoints.description: G3 the viewports rendered — mobile, tablet AND desktop are all required (names, not file paths).

rendered.description: G3 MUST be true: captured from a RENDERED page (Chrome navigation or Figma MCP), held in session. Building from .tpl/source markup alone is FORBIDDEN — anything other than true is schema-invalid and blocks all code.

properties_captured.description: G5 the computed-style properties actually read per element, held in the orchestrator's session for planning + verification. MUST include the visual-weight set the fidelity score depends on: color, background, font-family, font-size, font-weight, line-height, letter-spacing, padding, margin, gap, width, height, border, border-radius, box-shadow, opacity, text-align, direction, and icon stroke-width/size.

interactive_state_matrix.description: FROZEN Phase-A artifact (2a), held in session as structured text (NOT a repo file). Per element, every state it can be in, at each breakpoint. visual-verifier/qa-tester must exercise EVERY entry; an unexercised state is an automatic FAIL.

functionality_inventory.description: G4 FROZEN Phase-A scope contract (2b). EVERY link/control/state/form/endpoint/analytics/seo item. The planner MUST turn each into a phase or acceptance check. Silent scope narrowing is FORBIDDEN — a dropped item REQUIRES status 'waived' with a human-confirmed waiver_reason. The N13 gate MUST REFUSE to close while any item is neither 'done' nor 'waived'.

kind.description: 'analytics' = a legacy GA/track() event the page fires (assert track() parity in Phase C). 'seo' = a head-metadata affordance the legacy page had (title/meta/canonical/lang/dir/OG/JSON-LD) whose parity must be reproduced. Both are gate-blocking inventory items — the N13 gate cannot close while either is still 'todo'.

target.description: for a link: the href/route it points at

target_kind.description: for a link: whether it resolves to a frontend route or a legacy path

phase.description: the PLAN phase that satisfies this item

fidelity.description: The FOUR-AXIS success bar. Each axis is measured and reported SEPARATELY — never averaged into one number. A page is 'done' only when all four axes ≥ target (or the shortfall is human-waived).

compare_against.description: What the UI/UX diff table is measured against (the design-truth baseline).

axes.description: The four separately-measured scores. Never collapse to one.

ui_ux.description: computed-style + DOM diff across ALL states × breakpoints, RTL-correct. visual-verifier.

target.description: 0.98 gating. null = REPORT-ONLY vs the LEGACY look only, valid solely for a human-declared redesign — the page is still gated ≥0.98 vs the new design-truth artifact.

diff_table.description: the per-element/per-state diff, returned inline in visual-verifier's report (session, not a repo file)

code_logic.description: behavior/branching/state transitions reproduced (mapped, not transliterated). qa-tester + code-reviewer.

evidence.description: path to the branch-coverage / test evidence

code_structure.description: architecture/structure conformance, scored SEPARATELY from code_logic. container/presenter split; the src/api triad for all server state; @/* alias; import type; no `any`; Zod at boundaries; correct file/role placement with NO files-and-folders-naming-rules violation; no duplication of existing components/hooks; SEO/SSR head-metadata parity. code-reviewer scores it as (conformant checks / total checks).

evidence.description: path to the code-reviewer structure-conformance checklist result (per-check pass/fail with file:line)

functionality.description: every link/control/form/endpoint works end-to-end. qa-tester + integration-tester. Derived from functionality_inventory done/total.

evidence.description: path to the in-browser drive log / nav+network evidence

route_integrity.description: STEP 4b output. Per href × environment: does it resolve, is it frontend/legacy, does it behave. Reconciled against the ingress allowlists.

relative.description: deployed builds must keep cross-app links relative; a hardcoded cross-env origin is a failure

shared_modules.description: EXTRACT-ONCE REGISTRY for legacy code reused across MORE THAN ONE page — a shared PHP service/model, a shared jQuery util, a shared .tpl partial, a shared validation rule. The FIRST run to touch a shared dependency migrates it into a shared frontend home and records it here; LATER runs REUSE the recorded home and MUST NOT re-migrate it (that is how the same model gets migrated five inconsistent ways). legacy-decompiler flags candidates (a symbol whose legacy definition lives OUTSIDE this run's legacy_source.path yet is referenced by it); pattern-mapper decides the shared frontend home; the orchestrator reconciles against OTHER runs' shared_modules before building. A shared module claimed 'migrating' by another live run STOPS this run to a human decision (cross-run lock), exactly like locked_paths.

legacy_symbol.description: the shared legacy definition — function/class/service/partial name AND its file:line, e.g. 'formatSalary() assets/js/common/format.js:42' or 'Company entity application/models/Company.php'

legacy_path.description: the file the shared symbol is DEFINED in (OUTSIDE this run's legacy_source.path — that is what makes it shared). Recorded in legacy_source.out_of_scope_reads too.

used_by.description: the legacy pages/routes known to consume it — the evidence it is shared, not page-local. ≥2 consumers is the bar for 'shared'.

kind.description: what the shared thing is, which decides its frontend home

frontend_home.description: where it is (or will be) migrated to ONCE and reused, in an EXISTING repo home (all verified to exist): a shared src/api/<domain> triad + a src/types type for a model, src/components/shared for a .tpl partial, a src/hooks/use-* or src/lib util for logic, a src/forms/schemas Zod schema for validation, a src/constants entry for a constant. Named per files-and-folders-naming-rules. It is EXTENDED in place by later consumers, never forked.

migrated_fields.description: PARTIAL-MIGRATION ledger: the fields/methods/props of the legacy symbol actually migrated into frontend_home so far. A later consumer needing something not listed here EXTENDS the home in place (adds it) and re-runs the shared module's tests + earlier consumers' tests — it never forks a second copy. code-reviewer blocks a fork.

status.description: candidate (flagged, not yet decided) → migrating (THIS run owns it; a cross-run lock) → migrated (its frontend_home now exists) → reused (an EARLIER run already migrated it; this run imports it after a CONTRACT CHECK that it exposes what this consumer needs) → extended (a later run added a field/method the first migration lacked, in place, and re-verified earlier consumers) → drifted (the legacy symbol's legacy_sha256 changed after migration — re-open the shared module's Phase C AND flag every used_by consumer as blast radius) → waived (human-confirmed out of scope). Two live runs both 'migrating' the same id STOPS to a human decision.

legacy_sha256.description: hash of the shared legacy symbol's source at migration time. On any later run, if the live hash differs, status → 'drifted': re-open the shared module's Phase C and flag every used_by consumer whose behavior could shift, so the human sees the blast radius at the gate. A shared-logic change never lands silently across live pages.

owning_run.description: the run id that migrated (or is migrating) it — so a later run knows whose frontend_home to reuse

route_completeness.description: PER-ROUTE/PAGE structural completeness (STEP 4b). One row per in-scope legacy route/page: does a corresponding frontend route exist, in the CORRECT route group, with head-metadata (SEO) parity. The N13 gate cannot close while any in-scope legacy route lacks a matching frontend route or is placed in the wrong group. Completeness is tracked at the ROUTE level here, separate from the item-level functionality_inventory.

frontend_route.description: the src/routes/... path that satisfies it

route_group.description: the group the frontend route lands in; must match the legacy auth posture ($_SESSION guard → _private)

head_parity.description: true when title/meta/canonical/lang/dir/OG/JSON-LD parity with the legacy page is reproduced on the route

state.description: proposed (URL given at intake, shape not yet resolved) → mocked (MSW, shape inferred/labeled) → wired (real endpoint confirmed, DTO contract re-checked). 'drifted' = a wired endpoint whose legacy_sha256 changed after Gate C, re-opening Phase C.

devops.description: Route cutover is part of 'done' and spans BOTH envs. The route regex is appended to testing AND production values in the SAME diff; testing is applied now, production is prepared-but-not-live until human sign-off + the production code deploy. The N13 gate lists every env still lacking the route as an open blocker.

production_prepared.description: production-values.yaml path appended in the same diff, marked 'apply on sign-off AND with/after the prod code deploy' — prepared, not yet live

production_cutover.description: production path approved to go live (set at N13 'approved'); the developer commits it as its own commit

plan.description: The PLAN-APPROVAL gate between Phase A and Phase B. The planner presents PLAN.md in chat (phases + tasks + each phase's agentic loop + goal + design-system reuse/additions); Phase B MUST NOT start until the human returns 'approved'. 'changes' loops back to the planner.

next.description: The node to route next session.

design_system_inventory.description: FROZEN Phase-A artifact (2c). The design-system mapping for EVERY visual primitive on the source. Produced on EVERY run regardless of the declared case — a 'static'/case2 page changes the DATA wiring only, never the depth of extraction. Missing this blocks Gate A.

legacy.description: the legacy widget/class/glyph as it appears in the source

maps_to.description: the repo primitive to REUSE (src/components/... , shadcn/Radix component, cva variant) — reuse before build

reuse.description: build-new REQUIRES a logged reason; an existing primitive must be reused before a new one is written

tokens.description: the Tailwind/theme tokens the captured values resolve to

verify_states.description: the interactive-state-matrix states this primitive MUST be verified in (mapping is NOT 1:1)

drift.description: set when a captured value has no token in the scale — a design-drift flag to log, never a raw hex silently inlined

tokens_missing.description: captured values with no matching token — surfaced at N13 as design drift

extraction_contract.description: Seeded at intake. A declared case selects the BUILD workflow only and MUST NOT reduce Phase-A extraction depth. Present so no node can read 'static' as 'extract less'.

full_extraction_required.description: Always true. Extraction depth is constant across all cases and surfaces.

plan.description: The planner's output, presented in chat for human approval before Phase B. Phases each carry a goal tied to the phase's purpose, an ordered task list, and the agentic build->coverage->gate loop that satisfies them.

presented.description: true once the planner presented the plan in chat and asked the human to continue / add / consider / edit / remove.

goal.description: what this phase must achieve, tied to its purpose

agentic_loop.description: the build->coverage->gate loop + which nodes run + the cap

exit.description: the four-axis exit condition for this phase's slice

design_system_additions.description: Reusable design primitives (color, font, radius, spacing, shared component) that the source needs but the repo's design system does NOT yet have. Each is PROMOTED to a global token/component in src/styles.css @theme (or the shared components dir), NAMED per .claude/rules/design-system.md + files-and-folders-naming-rules, and only THEN used — never inlined as a one-off. Surfaced in the plan for human approval; react-synthesizer adds it before using it.

name.description: the global name to add, following the existing convention (e.g. a color ramp --color-<FAMILY><STOP>, --font-*, --radius-*, or a kebab-case shared component)

value.description: the token value (hex/px/font stack) or the component's source of truth

reused_by.description: the inventory items / elements that will consume it — justifies making it global rather than local

approved.description: set true when the human approves the plan that contains it
